mainEntity.name: How much does a Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fully rebuilt 2.0 TDI engine for a Tiguan Allspace typically costs £1,800-£3,200 supply-only or £2,500-£4,500 fitted. 2.0 TSI engines are slightly higher - £2,200-£4,000 supply-only or £2,800-£4,800 fitted. Used units start from £800 for TDI and £1,000 for TSI. DFGA/CRBC (150hp TDI) are the cheapest to replace - £1,800-£3,000. DNPA (245hp TSI) is the most expensive - £3,000-£4,800. DPF/EGR cleaning is £400-£800 if the engine itself is sound. All EnginesMarket quotes include 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF failure on a Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs include: a DPF warning light on the dashboard, a "Check Engine" light, reduced power during acceleration, increased fuel consumption, and in some cases, engine stuttering at idle. Some owners report the car entering limp mode when the DPF is severely blocked. Short urban journeys prevent DPF regeneration - regular motorway runs are essential. A forced regeneration (£120-£250) can often resolve partial blockages. If the DPF warning light flashes, get a diagnostic immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 2017-2019 Tiguan Allspace worth £8,000-£14,000, a £2,500-£4,500 engine replacement is borderline unless the vehicle is in exceptional condition with low mileage. For vehicles worth over £10,000, replacement is typically viable if the rest of the car is sound. The Allspace is a desirable family SUV - many owners choose to rebuild rather than scrap. Compare the cost of a rebuilt unit with warranty vs. buying another used Allspace. We always recommend a specialist inspection before any decision.

mainEntity.name: How reliable is the Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI or TSI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.0 TDI (EA288) is generally reliable with proper maintenance - DPF and EGR issues are the main concerns. The 2.0 TSI (EA888) is robust but prone to carbon buildup on intake valves and timing chain tensioner wear. With proper maintenance - regular oil changes, DPF-friendly driving (TDI), and walnut blasting (TSI) - both engines can exceed 120,000-150,000 miles. The 2.0 TDI is one of the most common diesel engines in the UK. The 2.0 TSI offers excellent performance but requires carbon cleaning. The 7-speed DSG (DQ381) requires oil changes every 40,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full engine replacement on a Tiguan Allspace typically takes 3-4 working days for a specialist (5-7 days for a main dealer). DPF/EGR cleaning is typically a 1-2 day job. Walnut blasting (carbon cleaning) is 1-2 days. Timing chain replacement is 2-3 days. Supply & fit providers may offer courtesy vehicle options.

mainEntity.name: Will a standard Tiguan engine fit an Allspace?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the Tiguan Allspace shares the same MQB A2 platform and engine range as the standard Tiguan. However, the Allspace is a long-wheelbase vehicle with different engine mount positions and electronics. Always ensure the replacement engine matches your Allspace's specific engine code (DFGA, CHHB, etc.) and 4Motion configuration. All Allspace engines are compatible with standard Tiguan of the same generation. 4Motion and FWD variants use different ECU calibrations. DSG gearbox compatibility must be verified.

historyTimeline.h2: Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI & TSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace - the long-wheelbase, seven-seat version of the second-generation Tiguan - was launched in 2017 to offer extra passenger and cargo space for UK families. Built on the Volkswagen Group MQB A2 platform, the Allspace shared its engine range with the standard Tiguan but with the 2.0 TDI and 2.0 TSI as the dominant powertrain choices. The 2.0 TDI diesel range included 150hp, 190hp and 200hp variants, while the 2.0 TSI petrol range spanned 180hp, 187hp, 220hp and 245hp outputs. All engines were paired with a 7-speed DSG automatic gearbox, with 4Motion all-wheel drive available across most variants.

milestones.description: Tiguan Allspace launched; 2.0 TDI DFGA (150hp) and 2.0 TSI CHHB (187hp) introduced
2.0 TDI CRBC (148hp) and 2.0 TSI CZPA (180hp) added
2.0 TDI DTUA (200hp) introduced; 2.0 TSI DNPA (245hp) added for facelift models
2.0 TSI DKFA (187hp) and DGU (178hp) introduced for facelift
Tiguan Allspace production ends; replaced by the second-generation Tayron

commonProblems.h2: Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI & TSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 2.0 TDI and 2.0 TSI engines in the Tiguan Allspace are generally robust - but they have predictable failure points. TDI models suffer from DPF and EGR issues, while TSI engines are prone to carbon buildup and timing chain tensioner wear. The 7-speed DSG (DQ381) can also develop mechatronic problems, often quoted alongside engine replacements. Rebuilt Tiguan Allspace engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF and EGR System Clogging - Why the Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI Suffers Emission System Issues
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI (all diesel variants, 2017-2024)
problems.typicalFailureMileage: 40,000-80,000 miles (urban use vehicles may fail earlier)
problems.rootCause: The Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) becomes blocked on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys where regeneration cycles are not completed. The EGR valve also accumulates carbon deposits, restricting airflow and causing limp mode. Symptoms include a DPF warning light, "Check Engine" light, reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and in some cases, engine stuttering at idle.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if DPF is partially blocked

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: DPF removal and cleaning, EGR valve replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if both systems are affected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt 2.0 TDI with new DPF and EGR
repairOptions.longevity: If DPF/EGR failure has caused turbo or engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2017-2020 Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI is worth £8,000-£22,000 depending on year, mileage, and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. DPF/EGR cleaning (£400-£800) is well within value for any running example. A full engine replacement (£2,500-£4,500) is viable for vehicles worth £10,000+, but for sub-£8,000 examples, evaluate scrap value before committing to a full rebuild.
problems.recommendation: DPF and EGR issues are the most common reason for engine-related warnings on the 2.0 TDI Allspace. If you use your Tiguan primarily for short urban journeys, ensure regular motorway runs to allow DPF regeneration. If you see a DPF warning light, get a diagnostic immediately - a £120-£250 forced regeneration is far cheaper than a full DPF replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DFGA Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: AdBlue System Failure - Emission System Issues on Post-2018 Tiguan Allspace TDI
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI (DFHA, DTUA, post-2018 models)
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue system - used to reduce NOx emissions - can suffer from NOx sensor failure, heater unit failure, or crystallisation in the injector. Symptoms include an AdBlue warning light, reduced engine performance, and in severe cases, a no-start condition.

repairOptions.longevity: If AdBlue failure has caused other engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: NOx sensor replacement (£300-£500) is well within value for any Tiguan Allspace TDI worth £6,000+.
problems.recommendation: AdBlue system faults are increasingly common on post-2018 TDI engines. Always use high-quality AdBlue and ensure the system is regularly serviced. If you see an AdBlue warning, address it promptly - ignoring it can lead to a no-start condition.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DTUA Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TDI engine prices

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - Performance Loss on the Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TSI
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TSI (all petrol variants, 2017-2024)
problems.rootCause: The direct injection system on EA888 engines does not have fuel washing over the intake valves, leading to carbon buildup from crankcase ventilation gases. Symptoms include rough idling, misfires, black smoke, reduced acceleration, and performance degradation. Carbon buildup is worse in engines that frequently run short trips in cold weather.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Intake manifold removed, valves cleaned with walnut media

repairOptions.longevity: If carbon buildup has caused valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Carbon cleaning (£350-£600) is well within value for any Tiguan Allspace TSI worth £6,000+.
problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a maintenance item, not a catastrophic failure. Budget for walnut blasting every 60,000-80,000 miles on 2.0 TSI engines. Using premium fuel and regular oil changes can help reduce the rate of buildup.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt CHHB Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TSI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Startup Rattle on the Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TSI
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TSI (all petrol variants, 2017-2024)
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can wear, causing chain slack. This results in a characteristic rattle on cold start when oil pressure takes a moment to build. If left unaddressed, the chain can skip teeth or break, causing catastrophic valve and piston damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chain, tensioner, guides, and sprocket replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early - rattle on start-up only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt 2.0 TSI with new timing components
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has snapped or caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Timing chain replacement (£550-£950) is well within value for any Tiguan Allspace TSI worth £6,000+. A full engine replacement is only justified on vehicles worth £10,000+.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattle on cold start from your 2.0 TSI Allspace, get it inspected immediately - a £550-£950 repair is far cheaper than a £2,800+ engine replacement. For higher-mileage examples, consider preventative timing chain replacement at 80,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DKFA Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace 2.0 TSI engine prices

problems.h4: 7-Speed DSG Mechatronic Failure - Gearbox Issues on the Tiguan Allspace
problems.affectedModels: Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace (all 2.0 TDI and TSI models with 7-speed DSG)
problems.rootCause: The 7-speed DSG (DQ381) used in the Allspace can suffer from mechatronic unit failure. Symptoms include harsh shifting, gearbox stuck in a single gear, and error codes. Some owners report combined engine and gearbox replacement quotes.
problems.vehicleValueCheck: Mechatronic replacement (£1,000-£1,800) is viable on any Tiguan Allspace worth £6,000+.
problems.recommendation: DSG issues often accompany engine problems because owners receive combined quotes. Regular DSG oil changes (every 40,000 miles) are essential for longevity. Software updates and oil changes every 60,000km are recommended.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Volkswagen Tiguan Allspace engine and DSG packages
